name: Vinaceous-Grey
lede: Vinaceous-Grey is a pink-tinged grey from Ridgway's 1912 bird-color atlas, measured at the same hex as our library's [[mauve-grey]].

sections.title: Two names, one hue
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 systematic nomenclature places Vinaceous-Grey on plate L, hue 69'''', tone d [1]. The ISCC-NBS revision of 1955 groups the same chip as "pale purple," block 227 [1]. Our library's [[mauve-grey]] sits at the identical measured hex, another case of two naming systems landing on the same color independently [2]. The next-nearest neighbor is [[irisglow]], a touch warmer [2]. Further out, [[platinum-grey]] and [[plumbago-grey]] sit in the same small cluster [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for Vinaceous-Grey in 149 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.6 percent, more common than 56 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 20 of 1,674 paintings, 2.4 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive [3]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a light tone, in 45 percent of its appearances [3]. John Singer Sargent carries it most often by raw count, 5 of his 287 paintings here, though at 2 percent of his output it does not clear the bar for a standout against his peers [3]. The earliest archive match dates to 1119, nearly eight centuries before Ridgway recorded the name in 1912, a look-alike hue, not proof of the name or pigment [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[3].
